Role: Fractional COO
Industry: Information Services
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Asana is the best project management software out there. I love that it focuses on perfecting functionality for a cohesive user experience. Task management across teams and projects make day to day work more manageable.
Cons: Sometimes there are limitations in functionality since Asana focuses on fewer features but perfects them rather than other products like ClickUp that have many features but are not perfect. Team adoption is a real challenge with Asana and really solid onboarding is required to get the most out of the product.

Comments: Asana is a great user-friendly interface that allows for easy task management and communication within projects.

Industry: Oil & Energy
Company size: 10,001+ employees

Overall rating: 4
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: It is somewhat limiting that a task can only be assigned to a single individual. While others can be added as “collaborators” by tagging their @name in the comments, I noticed this only after realizing that I wanted both people to review a document without creating separate tasks for each of them.
Cons: I really like the color scheme, the intuitive user interface, and the smooth performance. The mobile apps for individual use are excellent, and the platform is very beginner-friendly. That’s why I prefer it. I will definitely recommend this software to my agent. I’ve also already encouraged my friends and family to try Asana, and many of them are very satisfied, providing me with positive feedback. Additionally, the connectivity is seamless and reliable.
Comments: It’s very convenient to create tasks that are part of a project as well as [truncated]

Comments: I find Asana a very complete tool for Project Management, I used it for teams that work all remotely, even with different time zones, and even though it was small teams, so I couldn't use it to the full extent I really see how it can improve productivity and even change the way teams work.

Role: Project Manager
Industry: Writing and Editing
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 3
Pros: What I like most is the intuitive and clean interface. Even though it has a lot of features, it doesn't feel cluttered. Being able to switch between List, Board, and Timeline views easily is a game-changer because I can see my work exactly how I need to depending on the day.
Cons: While it’s very powerful, there is a bit of a learning curve at the beginning. It takes some time to figure out the best way to set up projects and workflows so things don't get messy, but other than that, all good.
Comments: My overall experience with Asana has been great. It has completely transformed the way my team organizes projects and handles deadlines. While it took us a little bit of time to get everyone comfortable with the interface and manage the notification settings, the clarity it provides is worth it. It’s a very visual, rewarding way to manage [truncated]

Role: Owner
Industry: Consumer Goods
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: I love the project management layout of being able to separate projects/tasks. It's a very easy to use software!
Cons: The UI is not the cleanest I've seen. It is good, don't get me wrong, but there are others out there have a better UI but worse features.
Comments: Great app, the free version has everything you need as a small/startup company, with room to grow and great prices for their other plans.
Reasons for choosing: Clickup had great reviews and their website was well made and good at explaining why it was different/better than other options.
Reasons for switching: Asana felt limited in a lot of ways, I wanted to see what else was out there
Switched from: Asana
Alternatives considered: monday.com AI Work Platform

Role: Small Business Owner
Industry: Consumer Services
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: ClickUp is one of the best tools on the market today. Their variety of templates available is incredible. My team and I use this tool for project management and CRM needs. They have a variety of plans to fit a variety of needs - from the free forever plan to a small teams plan priced at $7/user, a mid-size team plan priced at $12/user and an enterprise team plan. The available features on the free forever plan alone are incredible and include the ability to use unlimited tasks, have unlimited plan members, use whiteboards, enjoy real-time chat, and use many different views. Also included in the free forever plan is 24-7 support. I'm not aware of any other tool that has such a robust feature offering for a free plan. It's served my team and I very well with our PM & CRM needs at no additional cost. As a small business with a carefully [truncated]

Role: Process Manager
Industry: Machinery
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: ClickUp gives you so many ways to view and manage your projects—List, Kanban, Calendar, Gantt Chart, Timeline, and even more. It’s rare to find a tool that caters to so many different working styles. Also everything from task statuses to custom fields can be tailored. Whether you’re running a simple to-do list or a complex product launch with dependencies, ClickUp can be shaped to fit your needs. It feels like a tool that grows with you, no matter how sophisticated your workflows get.
Cons: ClickUp does so much that it can feel overwhelming at first. When I started using it, I spent a good chunk of time just figuring out what all the features did. It’s worth it, but if you’re someone who needs a tool that’s simple out of the box, you might feel frustrated.
Comments: ClickUp does almost everything, and it does most of it well. I like how [truncated]
